description:
Found s395 while doing #320 step 1 (adding capture_warnings to the stub).
Three helpers in perl-tests/t/test.pl MANUFACTURE a verdict:

    sub warnings_like (&$;$) { my ($code,$expected,$name) = @_;
                               $code->(); pass($name // "warnings_like") }
    sub warning_is    (&$;$) { ... same ... }
    sub warning_like  (&$;$) { ... same ... }

They run the code and pass UNCONDITIONALLY -- the expected warning is never
compared, and a test that emits the WRONG warning, or no warning at all, reads
as ok.  This is exactly the class #202 removed from cl/pcl-test.lisp (see
docs/tap-assertion-audit.md): a claim that cannot be evaluated must report
`not ok` naming the reason, never a pass.

It IS evaluable now: docs/not-supported.md records that `pl-warn` invokes
$SIG{__WARN__} correctly (only __DIE__ is missing), and the real t/test.pl
implementation is nine lines of plain perl (capture_warnings + a compare),
shipped by s395 as `capture_warnings` in the same stub.

POPULATION MEASURED (s395):
  perl-tests/  8 rows -- assignwarn.t (2 call sites in a loop), hashassign.t
               (4), time.t (2)
  companion t/ at least op/hashassign.t, op/assignwarn.t, op/utf8decode.t,
               op/time.t, op/inc.t, op/split_unicode.t, op/numify.t,
               re/subst.t

EXPECT ROWS TO GO RED, and that is the point (s393's `unlike` lesson: a
coverage decrease can be an assertion becoming honest).  Every row that flips
is a warning PCL does not emit or emits differently -- each needs a cause, not
a re-bless.

BAR: implement the three on top of capture_warnings, exactly as the real
t/test.pl does; then a full sweep + companion suite, per-file causes for every
row that flips, and the baselines edited row by row with those causes (never
re-blessed wholesale).  A row that flips because PCL does not emit a warning
perl emits is a FIX TARGET or a not-supported entry with an owner, not a
silently accepted regression.
subject: perl-tests/t/test.pl warning_is/warning_like/warnings_like manufacture a PASS (#202 class)
